residual connection.def: Adding a block's input to its output, y = ReLU(F(x) + x), also called a skip connection. The block only has to learn the change F, and gradients flow straight through the addition.

residual block.def: A block of layers F with a residual connection around it; the unit ResNets are built from.

projection shortcut.def: The shortcut of a residual block whose output shape differs from its input: a 1x1 convolution with the block's stride plus batch norm (downsample in torchvision).

basic block.def: ResNet-18/34's residual block: 3x3 conv, batch norm, ReLU, 3x3 conv, batch norm, add the shortcut, ReLU.

bottleneck block.def: ResNet-50's residual block: 1x1 conv from 4w down to w channels, 3x3 conv at width w, 1x1 conv back up to 4w (each with batch norm), add the shortcut, ReLU.

stage (resnet).def: One of layer1 to layer4 in a torchvision ResNet: a Sequential of residual blocks at one resolution. Each stage after the first halves H and W and doubles the channels.

torchvision.def: PyTorch's image library: standard models (torchvision.models), pretrained weights, datasets and image transforms. Installed in Colab.

imagenet.def: A dataset of about 1.2 million photos in 1000 classes; most pretrained image models were trained on it.

feature extraction.def: Transfer learning that keeps a pretrained backbone frozen and trains only a new head on its outputs.

channels-first.def: The (C, H, W) layout PyTorch uses for images; files, PIL and matplotlib use channels-last (H, W, C). Convert with permute(2, 0, 1).

image normalization.def: Subtracting each channel's mean and dividing by its standard deviation, (x_c - mean_c)/std_c; pretrained ImageNet models expect mean [0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std [0.229, 0.224, 0.225] on the [0, 1] scale.

baseline.def: The simplest reasonable predictor, such as the training mean (regression) or the most common class (classification). Every real model must beat its validation score.

noise.def: The random part of a label that no function of the inputs can predict, as in y = f(x) + noise.

normalized score.def: A raw metric turned into a number between 0 and 1. SP5 uses max(120 - MSE, 0) / 120, so MSE 0 scores 1 and any MSE of 120 or more scores 0.

results log.def: A table with one row per experiment: what changed and the validation score. It guides the next experiment and becomes the report.

noise floor.def: The lowest expected error any model can reach on new data because the noise cannot be predicted. For MSE it equals the noise variance.

periodic function.def: A function that repeats: f(x + P) = f(x) for every x, for some period P > 0.

period.def: The shift P after which a periodic function repeats. sin(2 pi x) has period 1.

fourier features.def: The columns 1, sin(2 pi k x / P), cos(2 pi k x / P) for k = 1..K: 2K + 1 columns. Linear regression on them gives a model that repeats with period P.

interpolation.def: Predicting at inputs inside the range covered by the training data.

extrapolation.def: Predicting at inputs outside the range covered by the training data, where the model's form, not the data, decides the prediction.

artifact.def: A file the training notebook produces that inference needs, such as learned weights, preprocessing parameters or a config. It goes in the submission ZIP next to submission.py.

pickle.def: Python's standard way to save almost any object as bytes (pickle.dump, pickle.load with files opened in binary mode). It stores an object's class by module and name, so the class must be importable when loading.

joblib.def: A library whose dump and load save and restore Python objects (built on pickle, efficient for big NumPy arrays). The cheat sheet uses it for fitted scikit-learn models.

sequence.def: An ordered list x_0, ..., x_(T-1) where order matters, such as the tokens of a sentence or the readings of a sensor over time.

sequence length.def: T, the number of positions in a sequence. A batch of sequences has shape (B, T) as ids or (B, T, d) as vectors.

token.def: The unit of text a model reads (a character, a word or a piece of a word), stored as an integer id. Also used for each position's vector inside a transformer.

tokenizer.def: The function that turns text into a list of token ids and back (encode and decode).

vocabulary.def: The fixed list of tokens a tokenizer knows; its size V is the number of rows of the embedding table and the number of outputs of a language model.

out of vocabulary.def: A word a word-level tokenizer never saw; it becomes the unknown token [UNK]. Subword tokenizers avoid this by splitting rare words into pieces.

subword tokenization.def: Tokenizing into pieces of words: frequent words are one token, rare words several. BPE (GPT) and WordPiece (BERT) are the two common kinds.

byte-pair encoding.def: BPE: build a subword vocabulary by starting from characters and repeatedly merging the most frequent adjacent pair into a new token.

wordpiece.def: BERT's subword tokenizer. It chooses merges by a likelihood score and marks pieces that continue a word with ##.

special token.def: A reserved id that is not text, such as [PAD], [CLS], [SEP], [MASK] (BERT ids 0, 101, 102, 103) or GPT-2's <|endoftext|>.

padding (sequences).def: Appending a pad id to shorter sequences so a batch forms one rectangular (B, T) tensor.

truncation (tokenizer).def: Cutting a token sequence that is longer than max_length down to max_length.

attention mask.def: A (B, T) tensor marking real tokens (1) and padding (0), in the Hugging Face convention. Pooling, loss and attention use it to skip padding.

collate function.def: The function a DataLoader calls (collate_fn=) to turn a list of samples into one batch; for text it pads and builds the attention mask.

masked mean pooling.def: One vector per sequence: the average of the token vectors at real positions only, sum(h * mask) / sum(mask).

recurrent neural network.def: RNN: a network that reads a sequence one position at a time, updating a hidden state h_t = tanh(W_ih x_t + W_hh h_(t-1) + b) with the same weights at every step.

hidden state (rnn).def: The vector h_t an RNN carries from step to step: its summary of the sequence so far. nn.RNN returns all of them (out) and the last one (h_n).

backpropagation through time.def: Backpropagation on an RNN unrolled over its T steps; the gradient to early steps is a product of one Jacobian per step, so it can vanish or explode.

lstm.def: Long short-term memory: an RNN with a cell state c_t = f * c_(t-1) + i * g and gates i, f, o. 4(HI + H^2 + 2H) parameters per layer in PyTorch.

cell state.def: The LSTM's second state c_t, updated by addition (c_t = f * c_(t-1) + i * g), which lets gradients survive many steps.

gate.def: A vector of values in (0, 1), made by a sigmoid, that scales another vector entry by entry to decide how much passes through.

forget gate.def: The LSTM gate f_t that scales the old cell state; d c_t / d c_(t-1) = diag(f_t).

gru.def: Gated recurrent unit: an RNN with update and reset gates and no separate cell; h_t = (1 - z) * n + z * h_(t-1). 3(HI + H^2 + 2H) parameters per layer.

bidirectional rnn.def: Two RNNs, one reading left to right and one right to left, with their states concatenated at each position (last axis 2H). Needs the whole sequence in advance.

attention.def: An operation where each query takes a weighted average of values, with weights given by a softmax of query-key scores.

query.def: In attention, the vector q of a position that is matched against every key to decide where that position reads from.

key (attention).def: In attention, the vector k a position offers for matching; its dot product with a query gives the score.

value (attention).def: In attention, the vector v a position hands over; the output is the weighted average of the values.

attention scores.def: The numbers q . k_j / sqrt(d_k) before the softmax, one per (query, key) pair; masks set some of them to -inf.

attention weights.def: softmax of the attention scores over the keys: nonnegative, each query's row sums to 1.

scaled dot-product attention.def: softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)) V, row by row. The scale keeps scores at variance about 1 so the softmax does not saturate.

self-attention.def: Attention where queries, keys and values all come from the same sequence, Q = X W_Q^T, K = X W_K^T, V = X W_V^T.

cross-attention.def: Attention where queries come from one sequence and keys and values from another, as when a decoder reads an encoder's outputs.

causal mask.def: The mask that lets position i attend only to positions j <= i: torch.tril of ones (allowed) or torch.triu(..., diagonal=1) (blocked).

permutation equivariant.def: Reordering the inputs reorders the outputs the same way and changes nothing else. Self-attention without positional encodings is permutation equivariant.

multi-head attention.def: H attentions (heads) run in parallel, each on its own d_k-sized projections; their outputs are concatenated and mixed by an output projection W_O.

attention head.def: One of the H parallel attentions in multi-head attention, with its own query, key and value projections of size d_k (usually d_model / H).

output projection.def: The linear layer W_O (H d_v to d_model) that mixes the concatenated head outputs in multi-head attention.

autoregressive generation.def: Producing a sequence one token at a time, each new token predicted from all earlier ones and then appended to the input.

kv cache.def: Stored keys and values of earlier positions, reused at each generation step. Size: 2 x layers x tokens x KV heads x head size x bytes.

multi-query attention.def: MQA: H query heads share a single key head and a single value head, shrinking the KV cache by a factor of H.

grouped-query attention.def: GQA: G key/value heads (G divides H); each group of H/G consecutive query heads shares one. G = H is MHA, G = 1 is MQA.

multi-head latent attention.def: MLA (DeepSeek-V2): cache a small latent c = W_DKV x per token; keys and values are up-projections of c, and those projections can be folded into the query and output projections.

positional encoding.def: Position information added to a transformer, which otherwise treats its input as a set: learned or sinusoidal vectors added to the input, or relative terms inside the attention scores.

learned positional embedding.def: An nn.Embedding(max_len, d) indexed by position and added to the token embeddings (BERT, GPT-2). Undefined beyond max_len.

sinusoidal positional encoding.def: Fixed PE[p, 2i] = sin(p w_i), PE[p, 2i+1] = cos(p w_i) with w_i = 10000^(-2i/d). A shift by k positions is a fixed rotation of each pair.

relative positional encoding.def: Position information that depends only on the offset j - i between query i and key j, for example scores q_i . (k_j + r_(j-i)); 2T - 1 learned vectors for length T.

alibi.def: Attention with linear biases: add -m |i - j| to each score, with a fixed slope m per head. No parameters; works on longer sequences than seen in training.

rope.def: Rotary position embedding: rotate pair i of q and k at position m by angle m theta_i. Then (R_m q) . (R_n k) = q . R_(n-m) k depends only on n - m. No parameters; not applied to v.

feature map (kernel).def: A function phi from R^d to R^l with sim(q, k) = phi(q) . phi(k); in linear attention it replaces exp(q . k / sqrt(d)).

linear attention.def: Attention with weights phi(q_i) . phi(k_j), computed as phi(Q) (phi(K)^T V) divided row by row by phi(Q) (phi(K)^T 1): O(T l d) time instead of O(T^2 d).

elu.def: Exponential linear unit: x for x >= 0, e^x - 1 for x < 0. 1 + ELU is a positive feature map for linear attention.

prefix sum.def: The running total s_t = x_0 + ... + x_t (inclusive) for every t; torch.cumsum. Causal linear attention uses prefix sums of phi(k_j) v_j^T and phi(k_j).

transformer block.def: The repeated unit of a transformer: multi-head attention and a position-wise MLP, each inside a residual connection with a layer norm. 12d^2 + 13d parameters with biases and d_ff = 4d.

position-wise mlp.def: The two-layer network Linear(d, d_ff), GELU, Linear(d_ff, d) inside a transformer block, applied to every position with the same weights.

residual stream.def: The running sum carried from block to block in a transformer: the input embedding plus every sublayer's update so far.

pre-norm.def: x + Sublayer(LN(x)): the layer norm is inside the residual branch, so the identity path never passes through a norm. Needs a final layer norm. Used by GPT-2 and most later models.

post-norm.def: LN(x + Sublayer(x)), the 2017 transformer's layout. Every path passes through a norm; harder to train deep without warmup.

weight tying.def: Using the token embedding matrix (V x d) also as the output layer's weight, so the output layer adds no parameters (GPT-2, BERT).

encoder-only model.def: A transformer whose self-attention is bidirectional (padding mask only), such as BERT; each output vector describes its token in the context of the whole input.

decoder-only model.def: A transformer with a causal mask in every block, such as GPT; trained by next-token prediction and used to generate text.

encoder-decoder model.def: A transformer with a bidirectional encoder for the input and a causal decoder that also cross-attends to the encoder outputs (original transformer, T5, BART).

bert.def: Bidirectional encoder representations from transformers: an encoder-only model pretrained by masked language modeling; [CLS] output used for classification.

gpt.def: Generative pretrained transformer: a decoder-only model pretrained by next-token prediction.

t5.def: Text-to-text transfer transformer: an encoder-decoder that casts every task as text to text, pretrained by span corruption.

masked language modeling.def: MLM: choose 15% of tokens, replace 80% of those by [MASK], 10% by random tokens, keep 10%, and predict the originals; loss only at the chosen positions (labels -100 elsewhere).

next sentence prediction.def: The original BERT's second task: predict from [CLS] whether sentence B follows sentence A. RoBERTa dropped it.

next-token prediction.def: The language-model objective: at each position predict the following token; targets are the inputs shifted by one.

teacher forcing.def: Training a sequence model on the true previous tokens instead of its own predictions.

span corruption.def: T5's pretraining task: replace random spans of the input by sentinel tokens and train the decoder to output each sentinel followed by its span.

sentinel token.def: A special token such as <extra_id_0> that marks where a span was removed in T5's span corruption.

ignore_index.def: The target value (default -100) that nn.CrossEntropyLoss and F.cross_entropy skip; the mean is taken over the other positions.

vision transformer.def: ViT: a transformer encoder applied to an image cut into P x P patches, each patch a token, plus a class token and learned position embeddings.

patch.def: In a ViT, one P x P square of the image across all C channels, flattened to C P^2 numbers. An H x W image has HW / P^2 patches.

patch embedding.def: The shared linear map from each flattened patch to a d-vector; equal to Conv2d(C, d, kernel_size=P, stride=P) followed by flatten(2).transpose(1, 2).

class token.def: A learned vector prepended to the token sequence (BERT's [CLS], ViT's cls); its final output vector is fed to the classification head.

inductive bias.def: Assumptions built into a model's architecture, such as a CNN's locality and weight sharing. Less bias needs more data; ViTs have less than CNNs.

language model.def: A model that gives the probability of the next token given the tokens before it; trained by next-token prediction.

perplexity (language model).def: e^(mean negative log-likelihood per token). A uniform model over V tokens has perplexity V; lower is better.

bits per character.def: A character-level language model's loss in bits: mean NLL / ln 2.

decoding.def: Turning a language model's next-token distributions into text, one token at a time (greedy, beam search or sampling).

greedy decoding.def: Always choosing the most likely next token (argmax). Deterministic; prone to repetition.

beam search.def: Decoding that keeps the b most likely partial sequences (by total log-probability) at every step.

temperature (sampling).def: tau in softmax(z / tau): tau < 1 sharpens the next-token distribution, tau > 1 flattens it, tau -> 0 is greedy.

top-k sampling.def: Keep the k largest logits, set the rest to -inf, renormalize, sample.

top-p sampling.def: Nucleus sampling: keep the smallest set of most likely tokens whose probabilities sum to at least p (including the one that crosses p), renormalize, sample.

pretraining.def: Training a model on a large unlabeled corpus with a self-supervised objective (masked or next-token prediction) before adapting it to a task.

linear probe.def: Training only a new linear head on the frozen features of a pretrained model.

full fine-tuning.def: Training every parameter of a pretrained model on the new task, with a small learning rate.

catastrophic forgetting.def: A fine-tuned model losing abilities it had after pretraining, because training on the new task overwrote them.

parameter-efficient fine-tuning.def: PEFT: keep the pretrained weights frozen and train a small number of added parameters (adapters, prompt tuning, LoRA).

adapter (peft).def: A small bottleneck MLP inserted into each transformer block and trained while the rest stays frozen.

prompt tuning.def: Training a few learned vectors prepended to the input sequence while the model stays frozen.

lora.def: Low-rank adaptation: freeze W and learn h = W x + (alpha / r) B A x with A (r x d_in) random, B (d_out x r) zero; r(d_in + d_out) parameters per matrix; merge W + (alpha / r) B A afterward.

qlora.def: LoRA with the frozen base weights stored in 4 bits, so a large model fits in less GPU memory.

hugging face transformers.def: The Python library of pretrained transformer models; Auto classes plus from_pretrained load a model and its tokenizer by name or from a local folder.

from_pretrained.def: The Hugging Face method that builds a model or tokenizer from a name (downloaded once into a cache) or a local folder; local_files_only=True or HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 forbids the network.

pipeline (hugging face).def: A wrapper that bundles tokenizer, model and post-processing for one task, such as pipeline('sentiment-analysis').

token type ids.def: BERT's tokenizer output that marks which sentence (0 or 1) each token belongs to when two sentences are packed into one input.

pooler output.def: BertModel's (B, d) output: the [CLS] vector passed through a linear layer and tanh.

text classification.def: Assigning one label to each text (spam or not, topic, sentiment).

document.def: In text processing, one text example: a sentence, a review, an article.

corpus.def: A collection of documents, such as a training set of texts.

bag of words.def: Representing a document by how often each vocabulary word occurs in it, ignoring word order.

document-term matrix.def: The matrix of shape (number of documents, vocabulary size) whose entry (d, t) is a count or weight of word t in document d.

sparse matrix.def: A matrix stored as only its nonzero entries and their positions (SciPy's CSR format); text features are mostly zeros.

term frequency.def: tf(t, d): how often word t occurs in document d (scikit-learn uses the raw count).

document frequency.def: df(t): the number of documents in the corpus that contain word t at least once.

inverse document frequency.def: idf(t), large for rare words and small for common ones; scikit-learn's default is ln((1 + n)/(1 + df(t))) + 1 for n documents.

tf-idf.def: Term frequency times inverse document frequency, usually with each document's vector scaled to unit L2 norm; down-weights words that occur everywhere.

n-gram.def: A run of n consecutive tokens; unigrams are single words, bigrams pairs such as 'not good'.

stop words.def: Very common words (the, a, of) that some pipelines remove before counting.

sequence-to-sequence.def: A task whose input and output are both sequences of possibly different lengths: translation, summarization, speech recognition.

decoder start token.def: The token an encoder-decoder's decoder reads first; for T5 it is the pad id 0.

bleu.def: A translation metric: the geometric mean of clipped 1- to 4-gram precisions of the output against the reference, times a brevity penalty for short outputs.

brevity penalty.def: BLEU's factor exp(1 - r/c) for a candidate of length c shorter than the reference length r; 1 otherwise.

clipped precision.def: In BLEU, the fraction of candidate n-grams found in the reference, where each n-gram counts at most as many times as it occurs in the reference.

exact match.def: The fraction of outputs identical to the reference (often after lowercasing and stripping punctuation); used for short answers.

rouge.def: Summarization metrics of n-gram overlap with a reference (ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2) or of the longest common subsequence (ROUGE-L), reported as recall, precision or F1.

sentence embedding.def: One fixed-length vector per text, trained so that texts with similar meaning have vectors with high cosine similarity.

retrieval.def: Finding the documents in a corpus most relevant to a query, usually by scoring every document and keeping the top k.

recall@k.def: In retrieval, the fraction of queries whose correct document is among the top k results.

mean reciprocal rank.def: The average over queries of 1/(rank of the first correct document); 1 when every correct document is ranked first.

lexical retrieval.def: Retrieval by word overlap between query and document (TF-IDF, BM25); misses synonyms and paraphrases.

dense retrieval.def: Retrieval by cosine similarity of learned embeddings; matches meaning even without shared words.

retrieval-augmented generation.def: Answering with a language model after retrieving relevant documents and putting them into its prompt.

open-weight model.def: A model whose trained weights are published, so you can run and fine-tune it on your own hardware (Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral).

api model.def: A model you can only query over the internet through a provider's interface, paying per token; its weights are not available (closed-source).

chat template.def: The tokenizer's rule for turning a list of role-tagged messages into one token sequence with the special tokens the model was trained on.

system message.def: The first message of a chat, with instructions that apply to the whole conversation.

zero-shot prompting.def: Asking a language model to do a task from an instruction alone, with no worked examples.

few-shot prompting.def: Putting a few worked input-output examples in the prompt before the real input (in-context learning).

in-context learning.def: A language model adapting to a task from examples in its prompt, with no change to its weights.

context window.def: The largest number of tokens (prompt plus output) a language model can process at once.

hallucination.def: A fluent but false statement produced by a language model, such as an invented function argument.

waveform.def: Audio as a 1-D array of amplitudes sampled at equal time steps (floats in [-1, 1] for most libraries).

sampling rate.def: Samples per second of a waveform, in Hz; speech models expect 16,000 Hz.

nyquist frequency.def: Half the sampling rate: the highest frequency a sampled signal can represent.

aliasing.def: A frequency above the Nyquist frequency showing up as a false lower frequency after sampling.

resampling.def: Converting a waveform to a different sampling rate, with filtering to avoid aliasing.

frame (audio).def: A short slice of a waveform (for example 400 samples = 25 ms at 16 kHz) analyzed as a unit; consecutive frames overlap.

window function.def: A taper such as the Hann window multiplied into each frame before the FFT, to reduce leakage between frequency bins.

short-time fourier transform.def: The FFT of each windowed frame of a signal; its magnitude over time is the spectrogram.

spectrogram.def: A time-frequency picture of a signal: the power (or magnitude) of each frequency bin in each frame.

mel scale.def: A frequency scale that matches perceived pitch, m = 2595 log10(1 + f/700): roughly linear below 1 kHz and logarithmic above.

mel filterbank.def: A set of triangular filters with centers equally spaced on the mel scale; multiplying a power spectrum by it gives mel energies.

log-mel spectrogram.def: The logarithm of mel filterbank energies per frame; the standard input of speech and audio models such as Whisper.

mfcc.def: Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients: a discrete cosine transform of the log-mel energies, a classic compact audio feature.

specaugment.def: Augmentation for spectrograms: masking random bands of time steps and of frequency bins during training.

hubert.def: A self-supervised speech encoder (Meta): raw 16 kHz waveform in, one vector per 20 ms frame out; pretrained by predicting cluster ids of masked frames.

whisper.def: OpenAI's encoder-decoder speech model: 30-second log-mel spectrograms in, text tokens out (transcription or translation to English).

audio-language model.def: An audio encoder whose outputs feed a text language model, so audio plus a text prompt go in and text comes out (Qwen-Audio, Voxtral).

generative model.def: A model of the data distribution itself, used to produce new examples that look like the training data (autoencoder-based VAEs, GANs, diffusion models).

autoencoder.def: A network trained to reproduce its input: an encoder maps x to a short code z and a decoder maps z back to a reconstruction x_hat.

encoder.def: The part of a model that maps an input to a representation; in an autoencoder, x to the latent vector z.

decoder.def: The part of a model that maps a representation back to data; in an autoencoder, z to the reconstruction x_hat.

latent vector.def: The code z = f(x) an encoder produces (or that a generative model samples); its entries are not labeled by anyone.

latent space.def: The set of all possible latent vectors z, usually R^k.

bottleneck.def: A layer narrower than the input (k < d) that forces an autoencoder to keep only the most useful information.

undercomplete autoencoder.def: An autoencoder whose code is shorter than its input (k < d), so it cannot learn the identity map.

reconstruction loss.def: A loss measuring how far the reconstruction x_hat is from the input x, usually squared error summed over coordinates (or per-pixel BCE).

denoising autoencoder.def: An autoencoder fed a corrupted input (for example x plus Gaussian noise) and trained to output the clean x.

anomaly detection.def: Flagging inputs unlike the training data, for example by a high autoencoder reconstruction error.

latent variable model.def: A model that explains each data point by an unobserved z: draw z from a prior p(z), then x from p(x | z).

latent variable.def: An unobserved random variable, such as the code z in a VAE, that a model uses to explain the data.

marginal likelihood.def: p(x) = integral of p(x | z) p(z) dz, the probability of the data with the latent variable averaged out; also called the evidence.

approximate posterior.def: A tractable distribution q(z | x), in a VAE a diagonal Gaussian from the encoder, trained to be close to the true posterior p(z | x).

diagonal gaussian.def: A multivariate normal with a diagonal covariance matrix, so its coordinates are independent normals.

log-variance.def: log sigma^2, what a VAE encoder outputs instead of sigma so that any real number is valid; sigma = exp(logvar / 2).

variational autoencoder.def: A latent variable model with a neural decoder p(x | z), a prior N(0, I) and an encoder q(z | x), trained by maximizing the ELBO.

elbo.def: Evidence lower bound: E_q[log p(x | z)] - KL(q(z | x) || p(z)). It equals log p(x) minus KL(q || true posterior), so it is at most log p(x).

jensen's inequality.def: For a concave f, f(E[Y]) >= E[f(Y)] (reversed for convex f). With f = log it gives the ELBO bound.

reparameterization trick.def: Writing a sample as z = mu + sigma * eps with eps ~ N(0, I) drawn separately, so gradients flow to mu and sigma through backpropagation.

posterior collapse.def: A VAE failure where the KL term wins, the encoder outputs the prior for every input, and z carries no information about x.

generative adversarial network.def: A GAN: a generator G(z) and a discriminator D(x) trained against each other; D separates real from fake, G tries to fool D.

generator (gan).def: In a GAN, the network G that maps noise z ~ N(0, I) to a fake sample G(z).

discriminator.def: In a GAN, the classifier D(x) in (0, 1) giving the probability that x is real; it outputs a logit in code.

minimax game.def: min over G, max over D of V(D, G) = E_data[log D(x)] + E_z[log(1 - D(G(z)))]: D maximizes, G minimizes.

optimal discriminator.def: For a fixed generator, D*(x) = p_data(x) / (p_data(x) + p_g(x)); it is 1/2 everywhere when p_g = p_data.

jensen-shannon divergence.def: JSD(p || q) = KL(p || m)/2 + KL(q || m)/2 with m = (p + q)/2: symmetric, 0 only when p = q, at most log 2.

non-saturating loss.def: The GAN generator loss -log D(G(z)) (BCE with fakes labeled 1), used instead of log(1 - D(G(z))), which is flat when D rejects the fakes.

mode collapse.def: A GAN failure where the generator produces only a few distinct outputs, covering a small part of the data distribution.

dcgan.def: Deep convolutional GAN, the standard convolutional architecture and recipe (Adam with lr 2e-4, betas (0.5, 0.999)).

diffusion model.def: A generative model that learns to reverse a gradual noising process: generation starts from pure noise and denoises step by step.

forward process.def: In a diffusion model, the fixed noising chain x_t = sqrt(alpha_t) x_{t-1} + sqrt(1 - alpha_t) eps_t that turns data into noise.

markov chain.def: A sequence of random variables where each one, given the previous one, does not depend on anything earlier.

noise schedule.def: The list beta_1 .. beta_T of per-step noise variances in a diffusion model (DDPM: linear from 1e-4 to 0.02 over T = 1000).

alpha-bar.def: alpha-bar_t = alpha_1 * ... * alpha_t; then x_t | x_0 ~ N(sqrt(alpha-bar_t) x_0, 1 - alpha-bar_t).

ddpm.def: Denoising diffusion probabilistic model (Ho et al. 2020): a diffusion model trained to predict the added noise with a plain MSE loss.

reverse process.def: The learned chain p(x_{t-1} | x_t) = N(mu_theta(x_t, t), sigma_t^2) that a diffusion model runs from noise to data.

noise prediction.def: Training a diffusion network eps_theta(x_t, t) to output the noise that produced x_t; the loss is ||eps - eps_theta||^2.

u-net.def: A convolutional encoder-decoder with skip connections between matching resolutions; its output has the input's spatial size.

time embedding.def: A vector encoding the diffusion step t (sinusoids, then an MLP) that is projected and added to the feature maps of each block.

ancestral sampling.def: Sampling a chain by drawing each variable from its conditional given the previous one; DDPM sampling draws x_{t-1} from p(x_{t-1} | x_t) for t = T .. 1.

ddim.def: Denoising diffusion implicit models: a sampler that predicts x0_hat and re-noises it to an earlier level with the same eps, deterministic and with 20-50 steps.

conditional generation.def: Generating samples that match a given condition c, such as a class label or text prompt, from a model eps(x_t, t, c).

classifier-free guidance.def: Sampling with eps_null + w (eps_c - eps_null), using one network trained with the condition sometimes replaced by a null condition.

guidance scale.def: The weight w in classifier-free guidance: 0 ignores the condition, 1 is plain conditional, larger follows it more closely with less variety.

null condition.def: A special 'no condition' input (an extra class or an empty prompt) used in classifier-free guidance training and sampling.

latent diffusion.def: Running the diffusion process in the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder, then decoding; much cheaper than diffusing pixels.

stable diffusion.def: A text-to-image latent diffusion model: VAE latents, a U-Net denoiser reading a text encoder through cross-attention, and classifier-free guidance.

object detection.def: Finding every object in an image and giving each a class and a bounding box.

bounding box.def: The smallest axis-aligned rectangle around an object; stored as xyxy (corners), xywh (corner and size) or cxcywh (center and size).

iou.def: Intersection over union (Jaccard index): area of overlap / area of union of two boxes or masks; 1 identical, 0 disjoint.

confidence score.def: A detector's score for one predicted box, used to sort predictions for NMS and for average precision.

non-maximum suppression.def: NMS: keep the highest-scoring box, delete the boxes overlapping it by more than an IoU threshold, repeat; done per class.

anchor box.def: A preset box shape at each grid position; YOLO and SSD predict offsets and scales relative to anchors.

yolo.def: You only look once: a one-pass detector that predicts boxes, objectness and classes for every cell of an S x S grid.

ssd.def: Single shot detector: predicts boxes from feature maps at several resolutions, coarse maps for large objects and fine maps for small ones.

detr.def: Detection transformer: a CNN backbone and a transformer encoder-decoder output a fixed set of box-and-class slots, trained with one-to-one Hungarian matching; no NMS.

hungarian algorithm.def: An algorithm for the one-to-one assignment of minimum total cost; DETR uses it to match predicted slots to ground-truth objects.

mean average precision.def: mAP: the mean over classes of average precision, the area under each class's precision-recall curve, at a stated IoU threshold (mAP@0.5) or averaged over thresholds 0.5 to 0.95 (COCO).

semantic segmentation.def: Giving every pixel of an image a class label; the output is logits (B, K, H, W) and the target a mask (B, H, W).

instance segmentation.def: Segmentation that also separates objects of the same class (car 1, car 2), usually with one mask per detected object.

panoptic segmentation.def: Semantic and instance segmentation together for every pixel of the image.

mask (segmentation).def: An array with one class id (or 0/1 for foreground) per pixel.

transposed convolution.def: nn.ConvTranspose2d: a learned upsampling layer; with kernel 2 and stride 2 each input pixel becomes a 2 x 2 patch, doubling H and W.

skip connection.def: In a U-Net, concatenating an encoder feature map with the decoder map of the same size, so fine detail lost by pooling reaches the output.

dice coefficient.def: 2|A and B| / (|A| + |B|) for two masks; 1 for a perfect match, 0 for no overlap; equals 2 IoU / (1 + IoU).

soft dice loss.def: 1 minus the Dice coefficient computed with predicted probabilities instead of hard masks, usually per class with smoothing and averaged over classes.

mean iou.def: mIoU: the IoU between predicted and true masks computed for each class over the dataset, then averaged over classes.

pixel accuracy.def: The fraction of pixels labeled correctly; misleading when one class (background) covers most pixels.

contrastive learning.def: Self-supervised learning that pulls together representations of two views of the same example and pushes apart those of different examples.

view (augmentation).def: In contrastive learning, one random augmentation (crop, flip, color jitter, blur) of an example; two views of one image form a positive pair.

positive pair.def: Two views (or an image and its caption) that should get similar embeddings; every other pairing in the batch is a negative.

simclr.def: A contrastive method: two augmented views per image, an encoder, a projection head, and the NT-Xent loss over the batch.

projection head.def: A small MLP after the encoder whose outputs z feed the contrastive loss; it is discarded after pretraining and the encoder's h is used.

nt-xent loss.def: Normalized temperature-scaled cross-entropy: for each of the 2N views, cross-entropy over the other 2N - 1 views of cosine similarity / tau, with the partner view as the correct class.

temperature (contrastive).def: tau in exp(similarity / tau); a small tau sharpens the softmax so the hardest negatives dominate the gradient.

masked autoencoder.def: MAE: hide most image patches (75%), encode only the visible ones, and train a light decoder to reconstruct the hidden patches' pixels (MSE on masked patches).

clip.def: Contrastive language-image pretraining: an image encoder and a text encoder projected into one space and trained with a symmetric contrastive loss on image-caption pairs.

zero-shot classification.def: Classifying into classes with no labeled training examples, for CLIP by comparing an image's embedding with embeddings of a text prompt per class.

prompt.def: The text given to a model as input; for CLIP zero-shot, a sentence such as 'a photo of a dog.' per class.

prompt ensembling.def: Averaging the embeddings of several prompt templates per class (then normalizing) to get a better class embedding.

symmetric contrastive loss.def: CLIP's loss: the mean of cross-entropy over rows (image to text) and over columns (text to image) of the similarity logits, with the diagonal as targets.

semi-supervised learning.def: Training on a small labeled set plus a larger unlabeled set from the same distribution.

pseudo-labeling.def: Self-training: predict the unlabeled data, keep confident predictions as labels (pseudo-labels), and retrain on them with the labeled data.

pseudo-label.def: A label for an unlabeled example taken from a model's own confident prediction.

confidence threshold.def: The minimum top-class probability for a prediction to be used as a pseudo-label, often 0.9 to 0.95.

confirmation bias.def: In pseudo-labeling, training on the model's own mistakes, which makes it more confident in them.

class-balanced selection.def: Keeping at most the same number of the most confident pseudo-labels per class, so an easy class cannot dominate.

consistency regularization.def: An unsupervised loss that penalizes different predictions for two augmentations (or noisy versions) of the same input.

mean teacher.def: A copy of the model whose weights are an exponential moving average of the student's; its predictions serve as consistency targets.

fixmatch.def: Semi-supervised method: pseudo-label from a weak augmentation if confident, then train the strong augmentation's prediction toward it with cross-entropy.

agent.def: In RL, the learner and decision maker: it observes states, picks actions and receives rewards.

environment.def: In RL, everything outside the agent; it answers each action with a reward and a next state.

state.def: In RL, the description S_t of the situation the agent observes at time t.

action.def: In RL, the choice A_t the agent makes at time t, from the set of allowed actions.

reward.def: In RL, the number R_{t+1} the environment returns after action A_t; the agent tries to maximize their discounted sum.

trajectory.def: The sequence S_0, A_0, R_1, S_1, A_1, R_2, ... produced by an agent interacting with an environment.

episode.def: One run of an episodic task, from a start state to a terminal state.

terminal state.def: A state that ends an episode; no rewards follow it, so its value is 0.

episodic task.def: An RL task that breaks into episodes that each end in a terminal state.

continuing task.def: An RL task that goes on forever without terminal states; it needs a discount factor below 1.

time step.def: One tick t = 0, 1, 2, ... of the agent-environment loop: the agent sees S_t, picks A_t, then receives R_{t+1} and S_{t+1}.

markov decision process.def: An MDP: states, actions and dynamics p(s', r | s, a) that depend only on the current state and action.

markov property.def: The next state and reward depend only on the current state and action, not on the earlier history.

dynamics.def: In an MDP, p(s', r | s, a): the probability of each next state and reward given the current state and action.

policy.def: The agent's behavior pi(a | s): a probability for each action in each state (deterministic if one action has probability 1).

deterministic policy.def: A policy that puts all probability on one action in each state, written pi(s).

stochastic policy.def: A policy that spreads probability over several actions in some state, pi(a | s) < 1 for every a there.

return.def: G_t = R_{t+1} + gamma R_{t+2} + gamma^2 R_{t+3} + ..., the discounted sum of future rewards; G_t = R_{t+1} + gamma G_{t+1}.

discount factor.def: gamma in [0, 1]: a reward k steps ahead counts gamma^k as much as an immediate one; 1/(1 - gamma) is a rough horizon.

horizon.def: Roughly how many steps ahead a discounted agent cares about, 1 / (1 - gamma): 10 for gamma = 0.9, 100 for gamma = 0.99.

gymnasium.def: The standard Python library of RL environments: env.reset() returns (obs, info); env.step(a) returns (obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info).

state-value function.def: v_pi(s) = E_pi[G_t | S_t = s], the expected return from state s when following policy pi.

action-value function.def: q_pi(s, a) = E_pi[G_t | S_t = s, A_t = a], the expected return after taking a in s and then following pi.

bellman expectation equation.def: v_pi(s) = sum_a pi(a | s) sum_{s', r} p(s', r | s, a) [r + gamma v_pi(s')]: a state's value from its successors' values.

backup.def: Updating a state's (or state-action pair's) value from the values of the states one step after it.

optimal policy.def: A policy whose value is at least as large as every other policy's in every state; it is greedy with respect to q*.

optimal value function.def: v*(s) = max over policies of v_pi(s), and q*(s, a) likewise; shared by all optimal policies.

bellman optimality equation.def: q*(s, a) = sum_{s', r} p(s', r | s, a) [r + gamma max_a' q*(s', a')] (and v* with a max over the first action).

greedy policy.def: A policy that picks argmax_a q(s, a) in every state for a given action-value estimate q.

dynamic programming.def: In RL, computing value functions and optimal policies from a full model of the MDP by repeated Bellman backups.

iterative policy evaluation.def: Computing v_pi by applying the Bellman expectation backup to every state repeatedly until the values stop changing.

sweep.def: One pass of backups over every state.

contraction.def: A map that shrinks the distance between any two inputs by a fixed factor below 1; Bellman backups with gamma < 1 are contractions, so iteration converges.

gridworld.def: A small RL test environment: an agent moves up, down, left or right between the cells of a grid.

policy improvement theorem.def: The policy that is greedy with respect to q_pi is at least as good as pi in every state.

policy iteration.def: Alternating full policy evaluation with greedy policy improvement until the policy stops changing; it ends at an optimal policy.

value iteration.def: Repeating the Bellman optimality backup V(s) <- max_a sum p [r + gamma V(s')] until convergence, then acting greedily.

model-free.def: An RL method that learns from experienced transitions without knowing (or learning) the dynamics p(s', r | s, a).

prediction (rl).def: Estimating the value function v_pi or q_pi of a fixed policy, as opposed to control (finding a good policy).

first-visit mc.def: Monte Carlo prediction that averages, per episode, only the return after the first visit to each state.

every-visit mc.def: Monte Carlo prediction that averages the returns after every visit to each state.

incremental mean.def: Updating an average in place: mean <- mean + (x - mean) / n; with a constant step alpha instead of 1/n it tracks a moving target.

step size.def: alpha in an update V <- V + alpha (target - V): how far each estimate moves toward its target.

exploring starts.def: Starting episodes at random state-action pairs so that every pair gets visited, for Monte Carlo estimation of q.

td(0).def: Temporal-difference prediction: after each step, V(S_t) <- V(S_t) + alpha [R_{t+1} + gamma V(S_{t+1}) - V(S_t)].

td target.def: R_{t+1} + gamma V(S_{t+1}) (just R_{t+1} if S_{t+1} is terminal): the one-step estimate of the return that TD moves toward.

td error.def: delta_t = R_{t+1} + gamma V(S_{t+1}) - V(S_t), the difference between the TD target and the current estimate.

bootstrapping.def: In RL, updating an estimate from other current estimates (as TD and DP do) instead of from complete returns.

temporal-difference learning.def: Model-free learning from each step's reward plus the current estimate of the next state's value (TD(0), SARSA, Q-learning).

control (rl).def: Finding a good (ideally optimal) policy, as opposed to prediction (evaluating a fixed policy).

exploration.def: Taking actions to learn more about them, possibly giving up reward now.

exploitation.def: Taking the action that currently looks best to collect reward.

epsilon-greedy policy.def: With probability eps pick a uniformly random action (from all actions), otherwise a greedy one; the greedy action then has probability 1 - eps + eps/|A|.

sarsa.def: On-policy TD control: Q(S, A) <- Q(S, A) + alpha [R + gamma Q(S', A') - Q(S, A)], with A' the action actually taken next.

q-learning.def: Off-policy TD control: Q(S, A) <- Q(S, A) + alpha [R + gamma max_a Q(S', a) - Q(S, A)]; it estimates q* while behaving epsilon-greedily.

on-policy.def: Learning the values of the same policy that generates the data (SARSA).

off-policy.def: Learning the values of a target policy (often greedy) from data generated by a different behavior policy (Q-learning, DQN).

behavior policy.def: The policy that actually chooses the actions and so generates the data.

target policy.def: The policy whose value function is being learned; in Q-learning, the greedy policy.

cliff walk.def: A 4 by 12 gridworld with a cliff along the bottom edge (reward -100); the standard example separating Q-learning from SARSA.

function approximation.def: Representing a value function (or policy) by a parameterized function such as a linear model or neural network instead of a table.

generalization (rl).def: Updating the weights for one state also changes the estimates for similar states, so the agent can value states it has never visited.

prediction objective.def: VE(w) = sum_s mu(s) [v_pi(s) - v_hat(s, w)]^2, the squared value error weighted by how often each state occurs.

semi-gradient method.def: An update that differentiates only the prediction and treats a bootstrapped target as a constant (detach it in code).

deadly triad.def: Function approximation, bootstrapping and off-policy learning together, which can make value estimates diverge.

deep q-network.def: DQN: Q-learning with a neural network Q(s, . ; theta), trained on replayed mini-batches against a periodically copied target network.

experience replay.def: Storing transitions in a buffer and training on random mini-batches from it, which breaks correlations and reuses data.

replay buffer.def: The store of recent transitions (s, a, r, s', done) that experience replay samples from; often a deque with a maxlen.

target network.def: A copy of the Q-network, synced every C steps, used to compute DQN targets so that they do not move with every update.

policy gradient method.def: An RL method that learns a parameterized policy pi(a | s, theta) directly by gradient ascent on the expected return.

softmax policy.def: pi(a | s) = softmax of per-action scores (action preferences) computed by a network; the RL version of a classifier's logits.

action preferences.def: The per-action scores h(s, a, theta) whose softmax gives a softmax policy's probabilities.

log-derivative trick.def: grad E_{x ~ p_theta}[f(x)] = E[f(x) grad log p_theta(x)], from grad p = p grad log p; the basis of REINFORCE.

score function.def: grad log pi(a | s, theta); its expectation under pi is 0. For a softmax over logits it is one_hot(a) - pi.

reward-to-go.def: G_t, the return from step t on, used in place of the whole-episode return G_0 to weight grad log pi(A_t | S_t).

reinforce.def: Monte Carlo policy gradient: after each episode, theta <- theta + alpha (G_t - b) grad log pi(A_t | S_t, theta) for every step t.

baseline (rl).def: A function b(s) subtracted from the return in a policy gradient; it keeps the estimate unbiased and can cut its variance.

advantage.def: q(s, a) - v(s): how much better action a is than the policy's average in s; G_t - v_hat(S_t) estimates it.

partial differential equation.def: PDE: an equation relating an unknown function of several variables to its partial derivatives, such as the heat equation u_t = alpha u_xx.

heat equation.def: The PDE u_t = alpha u_xx for the temperature u(t, x) of a rod; alpha > 0 is the diffusivity.

diffusivity.def: The constant alpha > 0 in the heat equation; larger alpha means heat spreads and decays faster.

initial condition.def: IC: the required values of a PDE's solution at the starting time, such as u(0, x) = sin(pi x).

boundary condition.def: BC: the required values of a PDE's solution on the edge of the domain for all times, such as u(t, 0) = u(t, 1) = 0.

analytic solution.def: A solution written as an explicit formula, such as exp(-alpha pi^2 t) sin(pi x) for the heat equation with a sine initial condition.

physics-informed neural network.def: PINN: a network u_theta(t, x) trained so that its PDE residual (computed with autograd) and its initial and boundary errors are small; the physics is in the loss, not the architecture.

pde residual.def: How far a candidate function is from satisfying a PDE at a point, for the heat equation u_t - alpha u_xx; a PINN minimizes its mean square.

collocation points.def: Points sampled from the domain where a PINN's PDE residual is evaluated; they need no labels.

forward problem.def: Computing the data a model produces from known parameters, such as the field of a known source.

inverse problem.def: Recovering a model's unknown parameters from (noisy) data it produced, such as a source position from field measurements.

nonlinear least squares.def: Choosing parameters theta to minimize sum_i (y_i - g(x_i; theta))^2 when g is nonlinear in theta; solved iteratively from a starting guess (scipy.optimize.curve_fit).

amortized inference.def: Training a network to map data directly to parameters, so the cost of fitting is paid once in training instead of once per sample.

fourier transform.def: Writing a signal as a sum of sines and cosines; np.fft.rfft computes it for evenly spaced real samples, and np.fft.rfftfreq gives each coefficient's frequency.

identifiable.def: A parameter is identifiable when different values of it produce different data; in y = p q x only the product p q is.

canonical form.def: One agreed representative among parameter values that give the same function, such as c0 > 0 and 0 <= c2 < 2 pi for c0 sin(c1 x + c2).

central field.def: A vector field F(r) = f(|r - r_s|) (r - r_s)/|r - r_s| that points along the line through a source r_s everywhere; f is the radial profile.

time series.def: A sequence of measurements in time order; a univariate dataset has shape (N, L), a multivariate one (N, C, L).

univariate.def: One measured number per time step (one channel).

multivariate.def: Several measured numbers per time step (several channels, such as several sensors).

per-series z-normalization.def: Subtracting each series' own mean and dividing by its own standard deviation, X.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True); removes offset and gain differences.

macro f1.def: The plain mean of the per-class F1 scores, f1_score(y, p, average='macro'); always predicting the majority class scores at most about 0.5 for two classes.

gpu.def: Graphics processing unit: a processor that runs thousands of arithmetic operations in parallel; PyTorch calls an NVIDIA GPU 'cuda'. Round 2 uses Colab's L4.

mixed precision.def: Running most matrix products in a 2-byte float format (bfloat16 or float16) while keeping weights and sensitive steps in float32; torch.autocast manages it.

bfloat16.def: A 2-byte float format with float32's exponent range and about 3 significant digits; needs no gradient scaling.

float16.def: A 2-byte float format with a small range (smallest normal number about 6e-5); small gradients underflow, so it is used with a GradScaler.

gradscaler.def: torch.amp.GradScaler: multiplies the loss by a large factor before backward and divides the gradients by it before the step, so float16 gradients do not underflow.

cuda out of memory.def: The error when tensors do not fit in GPU memory; reduce the batch size, delete unused tensors, or restart the runtime.

non-open-ended problem.def: A Round 2 problem made of fixed parts with definite answers (derivations, shape and count questions, modules to implement, a training part), each part scored on its own.

sample submission.def: The file an open-ended problem gives to show the exact prediction format: column names, row ids and their order. Your CSV must match it.

terminal.def: A text window where you type commands and read their output.

shell.def: The program inside a terminal that reads each command line and runs it; Ubuntu's default is bash.

bash.def: The standard shell on Ubuntu and most Linux systems.

option (command line).def: An argument starting with - or -- that changes what a command does, such as -l in ls -l. Also called a flag.

directory.def: A folder: a named container for files and other directories.

root directory.def: The top of the Linux file tree, written /. Every absolute path starts there.

path.def: The name of a file or directory in the file tree, with directories separated by /.

absolute path.def: A path that starts at the root directory, such as /tmp/ioai/train.py.

relative path.def: A path read from the working directory, such as data/train.csv or ../models.

working directory.def: The directory the shell is in right now; pwd prints it and relative paths start from it.

home directory.def: Your own directory, /home/ followed by your user name, written ~. cd with no argument goes there.

hidden file.def: A file whose name starts with a dot, such as .gitignore; ls shows it only with -a.

file permissions.def: Read, write and execute rights for a file's owner, its group and everyone else; ls -l shows them and chmod changes them.

owner (file).def: The user a file belongs to; the first set of permissions applies to this user.

group (file).def: The group of users a file belongs to; the second set of permissions applies to its members.

root user.def: The administrator account of a Linux system, allowed to change any file; sudo runs one command as root.

process.def: A running program. Each one has a PID and belongs to a user.

pid.def: Process ID: the number the system gives a running process; kill PID stops it.

pipe.def: The | symbol between two commands: the output of the first becomes the input of the second.

redirection.def: Sending a command's output to a file: > replaces the file's contents, >> appends to them.

version control.def: Keeping the history of a project's files so that any earlier version can be seen or restored.

git.def: The standard version control tool; it stores a project's history as a chain of commits.

repository.def: A project folder whose history Git tracks, kept in a hidden .git folder inside it. Also called a repo.

commit.def: A saved snapshot of the tracked files, with a message, an author, a date and a commit hash.

commit hash.def: The ID of a commit: 40 hexadecimal characters computed from its contents, usually shown as the first 7.

working tree.def: The files on disk in a repository, the version you edit.

staging area.def: Git's snapshot of what the next commit will contain; git add copies files into it. Also called the index.

head (git).def: Git's name for the commit you are on, usually the newest commit of the current branch. HEAD~1 is the commit before it.

untracked file.def: A file in the working tree that Git has never been told to track; git status lists it with ??.

remote.def: Another copy of a repository, usually on GitHub, that you push commits to and pull commits from.

origin.def: The default name Git gives the remote a repository was cloned from.

server.def: A computer that other computers connect to over the network, such as a shared GPU machine.

ssh.def: Secure shell: an encrypted connection to another computer that gives you a shell on it.

host.def: The name or address of a computer on a network, such as gpu01.example.org.

port.def: A numbered entry point on a computer; each network service listens on its own (SSH on 22 by default).

key pair.def: Two files made together for SSH: a private key that stays with you and a public key you give to servers.

private key.def: The secret half of a key pair. Never share it; keep it at permission 600 or ssh refuses to use it.

public key.def: The shareable half of a key pair; a server that lists it lets in whoever holds the matching private key.

ssh config.def: The file ~/.ssh/config, where a short alias can stand for a host, user, port and key.

tmux.def: A program that keeps shell sessions running on a server after you disconnect; reattach later with tmux attach.

nohup.def: A command prefix that makes a program ignore the hangup signal, so it keeps running after the session ends.

environment variable.def: A named setting that a program inherits from the shell, such as CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.

jupyterlab.def: The browser interface for Jupyter notebooks, with tabs, a file browser and a terminal.

kernel (jupyter).def: The process that runs a notebook's code and holds its variables; restarting it clears them.

port forwarding.def: Carrying connections to a port on one machine through an SSH connection to a port on another (ssh -L).

kaggle.def: A website that hosts data-science competitions with public and private leaderboards.

code competition.def: A competition where you submit a notebook, which the host runs within a time limit to produce the predictions.

public leaderboard.def: The ranking by score on one part of the test rows, shown during a competition.

private leaderboard.def: The ranking by score on the remaining test rows, revealed at the end; it is the final result.

scoreboard a.def: IOAI's scores on the validation data, given after each submission during the contest.

scoreboard b.def: IOAI's scores of each final solution on the test data, computed after the contest; rankings and medals use only these.

ioai normalized score.def: Task points from 0 to 100: 100 (raw - baseline) / (Max_Score - baseline), with Max_Score the larger of 0.9 times the organizers' solution and the best submission.

overfitting the leaderboard.def: Choosing submissions by their public score until the choice fits the luck of the public rows; the private score then falls short.

shake-up.def: A large change in ranks between the public and the private leaderboard.
